answer:
At 10 bar(a), ammonia's latent heat of vaporisation is about 1166 kJ/kg, which is about 19.9 kJ/mol using M = 17.03 g/mol. Its saturation temperature at that pressure is about 24.9 °C (298.06 K).

I worked this out with CoolProp, which uses the Helmholtz-energy equation of state for ammonia. It is the vapour enthalpy minus the liquid enthalpy at saturation, 10 bar. Near this pressure the value changes by about 1.35 kJ/kg per 0.1 bar: it is 1167.5 kJ/kg at 9.9 bar and 1164.8 kJ/kg at 10.1 bar.

I did not check it against a second source, such as NIST tables. Standard tables give roughly 1166 kJ/kg near 25 °C, so they should agree, but I recalled that rather than checked it. I created no files.
